correctness.rationale: The exact recurrence from Hu--Song--Tan reduces same-parity ordering to an integral inequality. Its integrand decreases with \(s=y^2\), so the endpoint \(s=3\) suffices; convexity plus Jensen reduces the proof to the explicit positive factor \(B_n\), whose polynomial sign argument is valid for all \(n\ge4\), with \(n=3\) checked separately. Closed forms for \(J_3,J_4\) and the one-turn derivative argument prove the cross-parity ordering. The displayed Stirling expansion was independently spot-checked against the exact density through order \(n^{-2}\); differencing its first correction gives the sign change exactly at \(y=\sqrt3\). The package verifier also checks thousands of finite degrees but is not used for the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the exact maximal interval on which fixed-variance Student central mass is monotone along both parity chains, proves the endpoint is intrinsic through the first asymptotic correction, and yields a closed unique extremizer. This is a natural sharp phase result in an active anti-concentration problem.
residual_risks: The optimizer structure above the phase boundary is not classified.

final_claim: For variance-one Student laws \(Z_n=\sqrt{(n-2)/n}\,T_n\), \(J_{n+2}(y)<J_n(y)\) for all integers \(n\ge3\) and \(0<y\le\sqrt3\); \(\sqrt3\) is the sharp uniform endpoint because every fixed \(y>\sqrt3\) eventually reverses the inequality. Moreover \(J_3(y)>J_4(y)\) on this interval, so degree three uniquely maximizes central mass there.
limitations: For \(y>\sqrt3\), only eventual same-parity reversal is proved, not the full finite-degree optimizer map.
